Why this matters for SSC

Capitals, currencies, and languages are top-5 most-asked topics in SSC. The list below is curated to include all 193 UN members plus frequently-asked non-UN entities (Taiwan, Kosovo, Palestine, Vatican, Western Sahara).

---

A — All 193 UN Member States (focus: high-frequency SSC questions)

A tip for memorization: study them in groups of 10 by region. Use the currency + capital combo as one card. Use 4-5 mnemonics like ArgCAPL for Argentina (Buenos Aires — Peso — Spanish).

Notable: Currencies named after their countries (or close)

  • Indian Rupee, Pakistani Rupee, Sri Lankan Rupee, Nepalese Rupee (all "Rupee")
  • Dollar family: US Dollar, Canadian Dollar, Australian Dollar, NZ Dollar, Singapore Dollar, Hong Kong Dollar, Trinidad Dollar, etc.
  • Pound: UK Pound (Sterling), Egyptian Pound, Lebanese Pound, South Sudanese Pound, Sudanese Pound
  • Franc: Swiss Franc, CFA Franc (used by 14 African countries), CFP Franc (French Pacific)

Currencies with same name as the country

  • Bolívar — Venezuela (named after Simón Bolívar)
  • Dinar — many (Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Algeria, Libya, Tunisia, Serbia)
  • Riyal — Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman (Oman has the Rial)
  • Real — Brazil

D — Currency one-liners (with country/region mnemonic)

  • EURO countries (20 Eurozone as of 2024): Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain.
  • Same-name currency as country: Switzerland → Swiss Franc, UK → Pound Sterling, India → Indian Rupee.
  • Dollar = used in ~25 countries (US, Canada, Australia, NZ, Singapore, Hong Kong, Namibia, Barbados, Jamaica, Trinidad, Guyana, Suriname, Belize, Bahamas, Cayman Islands, Fiji, Brunei, Solomon Islands, etc.).
  • Rupee = India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Mauritius, Seychelles, Maldives (Maldivian Rufiyaa is close), Indonesia (historical).
  • CFA Franc (XOF and XAF) = 14 countries across West and Central Africa (Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, Togo = XOF; Cameroon, CAR, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon = XAF).
  • East Caribbean Dollar (XCD) = 8 countries: Anguilla, Antigua & Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent & the Grenadines.

---

E — Indian states / UTs in the question pool

  • Indian state "neighbouring countries": Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka (across the sea), Maldives (across the sea). India shares land borders with 7 countries: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan. Note: India's border with Afghanistan is via PoK (Wakhan corridor). India has 15,106.7 km of land border.

---

F — Currency superlatives & trivia (SSC classics)

  • Most-traded currency in the world: US Dollar (USD).
  • Most-reserved currency: US Dollar.
  • Strongest currency (highest value per unit): Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD).
  • Most-fragmented currency area: Eurozone (20 countries).
  • Country with most currencies in use (de facto): Zimbabwe (USD, ZAR, BWP, ZWL).
  • Oldest currency still in use: Pound Sterling (UK) — since 8th century.
  • Country that first used paper money: China (Tang Dynasty, 7th century).
  • Country that first issued banknotes: Sweden (Stockholms Banco, 1661).
  • First country to decimalise currency: Russia (1704, decimal ruble).

Key concepts

  • 193 UN member states + 2 observer states (Vatican, Palestine) = 195 sovereign entities.
  • Euro is the most-widely-held reserve currency after USD.
  • Country that uses the most languages officially: India (22 scheduled + many others), Papua New Guinea (840 languages).
  • Highest currency value: Kuwaiti Dinar.
  • Capital: focus on those different from the largest city (Canberra, Brasília, Ankara, etc.).

2024–2025 Updates

  • Argentina (2024): Capital remains Buenos Aires; currency Argentine Peso (ARS). President Javier Milei (from Dec 2023) carried out aggressive devaluation; by 2024–25 the official rate vs USD was ~1,000 ARS/USD.
  • Syria (Dec 2024): After the fall of Assad regime, the new transitional government was formed. The capital remains Damascus. Currency Syrian Pound (SYP) (verify if any new currency is adopted in 2025).
  • Bangladesh (2024): PM Sheikh Hasina resigned in Aug 2024; Muhammad Yunus is leading the caretaker government. Capital Dhaka, currency Bangladeshi Taka (BDT) — unchanged.
  • Russia (2024): Capital Moscow; currency Russian Ruble (RUB). BRICS expansion (2024) added Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE, Saudi Arabia (though Saudi Arabia's status remained under review at year-end).
  • Eurozone (2024): Still 20 member countries; Croatia joined on 1 Jan 2023 (the 20th Eurozone member).
  • BRICS (2024): Expanded from 5 (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) to 10 members (added: Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, UAE; Saudi Arabia's status being negotiated).
  • G7, G20, NATO, SAARC, EU, AU: All as in the main lists above. Verify any 2025 changes on the day of exam.
  • Currency exchange rates (Jan 2025 approximate; verify on exam day):
  • 1 USD ≈ ₹84–86 INR
  • 1 EUR ≈ ₹90–94 INR
  • 1 GBP ≈ ₹105–110 INR
  • 1 KWD ≈ ₹275–285 INR
  • 1 BHD ≈ ₹220–230 INR
  • 1 CNY ≈ ₹11–12 INR
  • 1 AED ≈ ₹22–23 INR
  • 1 SAR ≈ ₹22–23 INR
  • 1 JPY (100) ≈ ₹55–60 INR
  • 1 PKR ≈ ₹0.30–0.32 INR
  • 1 NPR ≈ ₹0.62–0.65 INR (Nepalese rupee pegged closely to INR)
Caveat: Exchange rates fluctuate daily. For SSC, only the relative ranking matters (e.g., KWD > BHD > OMR > JOD > GBP > CHF > EUR > USD > CAD > AUD).
  • New country (if asked): No new UN member admitted in 2024–25 (Palestine and Vatican City remain observer states; Kosovo remains non-member, widely recognised).
Tip for SSC 2025: Lock in the 193 UN members + 2 observers = 195, the Eurozone 20 members, the BRICS 10 members, the NATO 32 members (Finland 2023, Sweden 2024), and the G20.
